titleEn: Poems on the Underground at 40: how Shakespeare inspired one of London’s best-loved public art projects
titleZh: 伦敦地铁诗歌四十年：莎士比亚如何启发一项公共艺术计划
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: If you have travelled on the London Underground at any time over the last 40 years, you’ll probably have noticed a poem or two. Perhaps on posters adorning the station concourse, or in tube carriages where adverts might normally be found.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你在过去40年中的任何时候乘坐过伦敦地铁，你可能会注意到一两首诗。也许是在车站大厅的海报上，或者是在通常会看到广告的地铁车厢里。

paragraphs.en: These poems are often unexpected, delightful and poignant. They remind commuters of our humanness and offer travellers small moments of respite. Whether on an empty platform or in a crowded carriage, Londoners and tourists alike can be moved by the rhythms of poetry.
paragraphs.zh: 这些诗歌往往出人意料，令人愉快和辛酸。它们提醒通勤者我们的人性，并为旅行者提供短暂的喘息时间。无论是在空荡荡的站台上还是在拥挤的车厢里，伦敦人和游客都能被诗歌的节奏所感动。

paragraphs.en: “I love dis great, polluted place,” says Benjamin Zephaniah in The London Breed (2001). “I sing of a world reshaped,” declares Nigerian poet Niyi Osundare with hope in I Sing of Change (1981). In A Bunch of Consolation (2023), Maura Dooley urges us “to love, to speak up, to hold steady”. A melancholic yearning for her mother’s cooking in Grace Nichols’ Like a Beacon (1984) – one of the first poems to be featured on a poster – beckons your appetite but breaks your heart.
paragraphs.zh: “我爱这个伟大的、被污染的地方，”本杰明·泽法尼亚在《伦敦的品种》（2001年）中说。“我歌唱一个被重塑的世界，”尼日利亚诗人尼伊·奥桑代尔在《我歌唱变革》（1981年）中满怀希望地宣称。在《一束安慰》（2023年）中，莫拉·杜利敦促我们“去爱，去说出来，在格蕾丝·尼科尔斯的《像灯塔》（1984年）中，一种对母亲烹饪的强烈渴望--这是第一批出现在海报上的诗歌之一--吸引着你的食欲，但却让你心碎。

paragraphs.en: This year Poems on the Underground has celebrated 40 years of bringing poetry to the commuting masses. The first poems to be displayed were Up in the Morning Early (1788) by Robert Burns; The Railway Children (1984) by Seamus Heaney; Like a Beacon (1984) by Grace Nichols; Ozymandias (1818) by Percy Bysshe Shelley; and This Is Just To Say (1934) by William Carlos Williams.
paragraphs.zh: 今年，《地下诗歌》庆祝将诗歌带给通勤群众40周年。第一批展出的诗歌是罗伯特·伯恩斯（Robert Burns）的《早起》（1788年）;谢默斯·希尼（Seamus Heaney）的《铁路儿童》（1984年）;格蕾丝·尼科尔斯（Grace Nichols）的《像灯塔》（1984年）;《奥兹曼迪亚斯》（Ozymandias）（1818年），作者：珀西·比希·雪莱（Percy Bysshe Shelley）;威廉·卡洛斯威廉姆斯的《这只是说》（1934）。

paragraphs.en: The project was the brainchild of the American essayist and novelist Judith Chernaik, who came up with the idea as a young academic when she moved to London in 1972 with her husband and children. The couple befriended the Barrow poets Gerard Benson and Cicely Herbert and soon became part of their literary circle. The Barrow poets were a group of writers and folk musicians who got their name from selling poems from handbarrows in local markets.
paragraphs.zh: 这个项目是美国散文家和小说家朱迪思·切尔奈克的创意，1972年，当她还是一名年轻的学者时，她和丈夫、孩子搬到了伦敦。这对夫妇与巴罗诗人杰勒德·本森和西塞利·赫伯特成为朋友，很快就成了他们文学圈的一员。巴罗诗人是一群作家和民间音乐家，他们因出售手推车上的诗歌而得名在当地市场。

paragraphs.en: The couple were invited to attend play-reading groups, and in one such gathering, the work being explored was Shakespeare’s As You Like It. Chernaik was charmed by the figure of Orlando, who hangs poems in the trees of the Forest of Arden for his love, Rosalind.
paragraphs.zh: 这对夫妇被邀请参加戏剧阅读小组，在一次这样的聚会上，正在探索的作品是莎士比亚的《如你所愿》。

paragraphs.en: Imagining the London Underground as a real-life contemporary Forest of Arden, she asked her friends what they thought of her idea to hang some poems in the advertising spaces on the tube. Delighted by the notion, they encouraged her, and the following morning, a determined Chernaik wrote to London Transport (later TfL).
paragraphs.zh: 她把伦敦地铁想象成一个现实生活中的当代雅顿森林，问朋友们对她在地铁广告位上悬挂一些诗歌的想法有什么看法。他们对这个想法很高兴，鼓励她。第二天早上，一个坚定的切尔奈克写信给伦敦交通局（后来的TfL）。

paragraphs.en: To her amazement London Transport replied and was interested in her proposal. She secured an Arts Council Grant in 1985 and the rest is literary history: four decades of sharing poetry with the public though Poems on the Underground.
paragraphs.zh: 令她惊讶的是，伦敦交通局回复了她的提议，并对她的提议感兴趣。她在1985年获得了艺术理事会拨款，剩下的就是文学史：四十年来通过《地下诗歌》与公众分享诗歌。

paragraphs.en: Literary academic Anna Barton has observed that in As You Like It, “the Forest of Arden is a place of freedom, transformation and love – but also hardship for the shepherds who work there”. But if Shakespeare was the inspiration for Chernaik, a scholar of Romantic poetry, the motivation came from her study of Percy Bysshe Shelley and John Keats.
paragraphs.zh: 文学学者安娜巴顿在《皆大欢喜》中指出，“雅顿森林是一个充满自由、变革和爱的地方--但对于在那里工作的牧羊人来说，也是一个艰难的地方”。但如果说莎士比亚是浪漫主义诗歌学者切尔奈克的灵感来源，那么她的动机则来自于对珀西比希雪莱和约翰济慈的研究。

paragraphs.en: Finding meaning amid the tumult
paragraphs.zh: 在喧嚣中寻找意义

paragraphs.en: Keats, who died at just 26, worried in his letters whether he would be read, while Shelly believed poetry had the power to change the world. Here was a project that could accomplish both things. Indeed, joined by Gerard Benson and Cicley Herbert who became co-founders of the initiative, the three brought to millions of passengers a wide range of poetry from the past and present, and written by poets from all over the world.
paragraphs.zh: 年仅26岁就去世的济慈在信中担心自己是否会被人读到，而雪莱则相信诗歌有改变世界的力量。这是一个可以实现这两件事的项目。事实上，杰拉德·本森和西克利赫伯特成为该项目的共同创始人，他们三人为数百万乘客带来了过去和现在的各种诗歌，由世界各地的诗人创作。

paragraphs.en: Today Cherniak’s co-directors are the poets Imtiaz Dharker and George Szirtes; after the death of Benson in 2014, Herbert stepped back. The programme has been so successful it has been replicated in cities such as New York, Paris, Beijing, Dublin, Moscow, Shanghai and Warsaw.
paragraphs.zh: 如今，切尔尼亚克的联合导演是诗人伊姆蒂亚兹·达克（Imtiaz Dharker）和乔治·斯泰尔特斯（George Spartes）; 2014年本森去世后，赫伯特（Herbert）退居二线。该项目非常成功，已被复制到纽约、巴黎、北京、都柏林、莫斯科、上海和华沙等城市。

paragraphs.en: In London, the tube rumbles to the rhythm of the best poetry in the world. One of my favourites is Oscar Wilde’s Symphony in Yellow, a poem first published in 1889.
paragraphs.zh: 在伦敦，地铁里隆隆作响的是世界上最好的诗歌的节奏，我最喜欢的诗歌之一是奥斯卡·王尔德的《黄色交响曲》，这首诗首次发表于1889年。

paragraphs.en: An omnibus across the bridge
paragraphs.zh: 过桥的公共汽车

paragraphs.en: Crawls like a yellow butterfly,
paragraphs.zh: 像一只黄色的蝴蝶一样爬行，

paragraphs.en: And, here and there, a passer-by
paragraphs.zh: 还有，这里和那里，一个路人

paragraphs.en: Shows like a little restless midge.
paragraphs.zh: 就像一只不安分的小蚊子。

paragraphs.en: When I first saw it on the tube, the poem transported me to the London of the 1890s. In the 19th century, omnibus routes were colour coded – how ingenious of Wilde to sing of the bus as a yellow butterfly. The design for the poem, which included an illustration depicting Oscar Wilde himself, made me aware of another aspect of the Poems on the Underground: their visual impact that comes from beautiful typography, use of colour and layout.
paragraphs.zh: 当我第一次在地铁上看到这首诗的时候，它把我带到了19世纪90年代的伦敦。在19世纪的世纪，公共汽车的路线是用颜色编码的--王尔德把公共汽车唱成一只黄色的蝴蝶是多么的巧妙啊。这首诗的设计包括一幅描绘奥斯卡·王尔德本人的插图，让我意识到了《地下诗歌》的另一个方面：他们的视觉冲击力，来自美丽的排版，颜色和布局的使用。

paragraphs.en: The poet Arthur Symons wrote in 1909 of the dehumanisation of passengers travelling on the Underground: “The creatures that we see now in the machines are hardly to be called human beings, so are they disfigured out of all recognition, in order that they may go fast enough not to see anything themselves.”
paragraphs.zh: 诗人亚瑟·西蒙斯（Arthur Symons）在1909年写道，地铁乘客的非人性化：“我们现在在机器中看到的生物很难被称为人类，所以他们被毁容得面目全非，为了让他们走得足够快，自己什么也看不见。”

paragraphs.en: For the last 40 years, Poems on the Underground has done the exact opposite: it has continually reminded passengers of their humanity. And Symons would probably have been thrilled to know A Tune (1899), his poem about the persistence of memory, would one day be displayed on the tube.
paragraphs.zh: 在过去的40年里，《地铁上的诗歌》所做的恰恰相反：它不断地提醒乘客他们的人性。西蒙斯可能会很激动地知道有一天他关于记忆持久性的诗歌《一首曲子》（1899）会在地铁上展出。

paragraphs.en: Seamus Heaney, one of the first poets to be featured, wrote to Chernaik in 1999 to say: “I admire you for keeping the underground poems a priority; it is worth doing and has made a difference, I am sure, to the life-worth of poetry for many people. Blessings on the work.”
paragraphs.zh: 谢默斯·希尼（Seamus Heaney）是第一批被选中的诗人之一，他在1999年写信给切尔奈克说：“我很钦佩你把地下诗歌放在首位;这是值得做的，我相信，对许多人来说，诗歌的生命价值已经有所不同。祝福这项工作。”

paragraphs.en: As the Poems on the Underground archive at the University of Cambridge attests, the project is much loved by the public and poets alike. It is a powerful example of the uplifting effect of the arts, and how bringing art into everyday public spaces can transform the experience of the people using them.
paragraphs.zh: 正如剑桥大学的地下诗歌档案馆所证明的那样，这个项目深受公众和诗人的喜爱。它是一个强有力的例子，说明了艺术的提升作用，以及将艺术带入日常公共空间如何改变人们使用它们的体验。
